sourceChecks.claim: AWS ELB introduction supports traffic distribution and backend targets; reverse-proxy return path is consistent with documented HTTP load balancing.
Azure overview supports L4 transport versus L7 HTTP paths/TLS offload; AWS NLB introduction followup verifies connection-selected targets, preserving reused-connection reasoning.
NGINX documents round-robin, active least-connections and weighted shares; work/capacity limitations are correct inference from these signals.
AWS health-check guide specifies intervals, failure thresholds and all-unhealthy fail-open. Sampled checks cannot establish application-wide success or repair accepted work.
Microsoft web-farm guidance describes per-node memory-state loss and distributed state; affinity preserves placement, not replication. Shared-store costs are architectural consequences.
AWS deregistration guide stops new requests, waits a configured delay and warns early termination errors; L4 connection caveat follows connection-level routing, not a promise of zero interruption.
AWS idempotent-API article verifies stable ID and atomic token/mutation outcome across retries; shared durable records and bounded delayed attempts implement that contract.

Google SRE overload chapter supports finite resource limits, shedding and downstream/retry amplification. Reachable redundant entry and survivor headroom are necessary system-level conditions, not automatic load-balancer guarantees.
